paragraphs.title: God as the Eternal Dwelling and the Transience of Human Life

easy.explanation: Psalm 90:1 calls the LORD the dwelling place of His people in all generations.
easy.q: What has the LORD been to His people in all generations?

easy.explanation: The LORD existed from everlasting, before the mountains and the earth were formed.
easy.q: What existed before the mountains were brought forth?

easy.explanation: The passage compares people to grass that grows in the morning and later withers.
easy.q: What is man compared to in the morning?

answers: God is everlasting, while human life is temporary
Human beings are everlasting, while God is temporary
Night is permanent, while day is temporary
medium.explanation: The LORD is eternal, but human life is brief and quickly passes away.
medium.q: What main contrast appears in verses 1–6?

answers: A division or period of the night
medium.explanation: A watch was a designated period during the night.
medium.q: In the phrase “as a watch in the night,” what is a watch?

answers: It begins at evening and lasts forever
It remains unchanged from morning to night
It flourishes in the morning and withers by evening
medium.explanation: Like grass, human life flourishes in the morning but is cut down and withers in the evening.
medium.q: How does the psalm describe the course of human life?

answers: Human time is very short compared with God's eternity
Every person lives for a thousand years
A night watch lasts longer than eternity
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes how brief human time is in God's sight.
challenge.q: What does the comparison of a thousand years to yesterday and a night watch suggest?

answers: They emphasize passing quickly and fading away
They describe a lasting dwelling place
challenge.explanation: Sleep passes quickly, and grass grows and withers, both illustrating life's transience.
challenge.q: Why are sleep and grass fitting pictures of human life in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The rapid movement from morning flourishing to evening withering portrays the brevity of life.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the movement from morning to evening?

paragraphs.title: Sin, Divine Anger, and the Brevity of Life

answers: Because of God's anger and wrath
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says that people are consumed by God's anger and troubled by His wrath.
easy.q: Why are people consumed and troubled according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The LORD has set people's iniquities and secret sins before Him.
easy.q: What has God set before Him?

easy.explanation: Psalm 90:10 speaks of seventy years, or eighty years if a person has strength.
easy.q: How many years are given as the usual span of life?

answers: Sins are exposed before God, so people are troubled by His wrath
Sins make human life last longer
medium.explanation: The knowledge that sins are visible before God is connected with fear of His wrath.
medium.q: What is the relationship between sin and human fear in these verses?

answers: Wrong things hidden from other people but known to God
medium.explanation: Even hidden sins are exposed in the light of God's countenance.
medium.q: What does “our secret sins” mean in verse 8?

answers: As labor and sorrow that quickly pass away
As unrelated to the passage of time
medium.explanation: Even a strong life is described as labor and sorrow, soon cut off.
medium.q: How are the accomplishments of human life described?

answers: Human years pass quickly like a brief account
challenge.explanation: The image presents life as something quickly spoken and finished.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “we spend our years as a tale that is told” suggest?

answers: Short life and God's judgment make faithful living important
Short life makes every action meaningless
Short life guarantees that sins will be forgotten
challenge.explanation: The verses join life's brevity with exposed sin and God's wrath, giving moral seriousness to life.
challenge.q: What connection do these verses make between short life and moral accountability?

answers: Even a relatively long life is still brief and temporary
Every person lives exactly eighty years
challenge.explanation: Strength may extend life somewhat, but it does not make life everlasting.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the statement that even the years of strength may reach only eighty?

paragraphs.title: A Request for Wisdom Through Awareness of Time

easy.explanation: Verse 12 asks God to teach people to number their days.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to teach His people?

easy.explanation: The purpose is that people may apply their hearts unto wisdom.
easy.q: What should result from numbering our days?

easy.explanation: Numbering our days means recognizing that human life is limited and temporary.
easy.q: What is the main subject of the request in verse 12?

answers: Counting our days reminds us that life is limited
Counting the days makes them longer
medium.explanation: Awareness of limited time should lead people to live wisely.
medium.q: Why is wisdom connected with numbering our days?

answers: It encourages meaningful and wise use of life
It causes people to ignore their actions
medium.explanation: Recognizing life's brevity can direct people away from worthless or sinful pursuits.
medium.q: How can awareness of limited time affect a person's choices?

answers: A world that never passes away
medium.explanation: The verse asks that people may apply their hearts unto wisdom.
medium.q: What result does the psalmist ask for after learning to number the days?

answers: To recognize that human life is limited
challenge.explanation: The expression represents awareness of life's brevity and limitations.
challenge.q: What does “number our days” mean in the context of Psalm 90?

answers: It turns awareness of life's brevity into a request for wisdom
It cancels the earlier teaching about death
It returns to the creation of the mountains
challenge.explanation: The psalmist responds to the shortness of life by asking for wise understanding.
challenge.q: How does verse 12 serve as a transition in the psalm?

answers: Awareness of time can influence human choices
Time has no effect on people
challenge.explanation: The verse assumes that recognizing life's limits can lead to wiser living.
challenge.q: What moral assumption lies behind the request for a wise heart?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Kindness, Joy, and the Establishment of Human Work

easy.explanation: The psalmist asks the LORD to return and show compassion to His servants.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: Verse 14 asks God to satisfy His people early with His mercy.
easy.q: With what does the psalmist ask God to satisfy His people?

easy.explanation: The closing verse repeatedly asks God to establish the work of their hands.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do to the work of his hands?

answers: God's mercy enables His people to rejoice and be glad
God's mercy cancels every human work
God's mercy causes people only to fear
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for mercy so that the people may rejoice and be glad all their days.
medium.q: What is the connection between God's mercy and joy?

medium.explanation: Verse 16 asks that the LORD's work appear to His servants.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask to see?

answers: The psalmist asks for God's glory to reach the next generation
They represent the shortness of the night
They are unrelated to the work being described
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for God's glory to appear unto their children as well.
medium.q: Why are the children mentioned in the request?

answers: The psalmist asks for joy to balance the years of trouble
The psalmist asks for more years of trouble
The psalmist asks to erase all memory of the past
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks God to make His people glad according to the days in which they suffered.
challenge.q: How is the request for gladness related to the years of affliction?

answers: A request for God's favor and goodness to rest upon His people
A desire for people to stop working
A request for time to cease passing
challenge.explanation: The phrase asks for God's gracious favor to be upon His people and their work.
challenge.q: What does “the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us” express?

answers: The desire for human work to be made firm and lasting by God
The cancellation of all human work
challenge.explanation: The repetition strongly emphasizes the plea for God to establish their work.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “the work of our hands establish thou it” emphasize?
